reviews.review: if you like left 4 dead you will like this

Back 4 Blood so far has been hit or miss. If you have friends to play it with or are fans of the Left 4 Dead series I would say the game is worth getting (only if its on sale). The games has problems with balance and the Ridden spawn rate especially Special Ridden which makes the game needlessly difficult on even the normal difficulty. The game design is also very questionable with a lazy starting hub that feels pointless and empty. Supply Decks are an absolute grind fest for honestly some crappy cards that do little to actually help in the campaign. This all feels like a way to artificially keep the game alive for a game that would be relatively short otherwise. Despite all that I do think this game has promise and can be better in the future and is a good time with some good friends.

No offline mode and no solo mode. Heaven forbid I want to play the game without random people online. Definitely not gonna convince my friends to get this dumb game. The difficulty curve is also a bit much. Nowhere near worth the price. Find a different game to play with friends or solo.

EDIT: Well I'll be damned, they added a solo mode. Imagine getting what was advertised after only waiting a few months hey. Still not worth the price, and honestly they have a rng based debuff where there is a mysterious fog or the lights go out and good luck finding anything with that. Just an idiotic excuse to lower quality of life. You can't even remove accessories, so if you see a nice deagle with a 2x scope just have to hip shoot for close range.

Is it a game? Is it a mad cash grab for nostalgia? WHY CAN'T IT BE BOTH?

TL:DR 
Back4Blood has got it's moments. If you've never played Left4Dead, then it is an absolute must play. If you've played L4D before and want a 2021 texture package slapped over it, then it's worth a play for sure. Finally, if all you want do is scream at your friends like it's 2008, from the safety of your childhood memory pillow fort, then this might be worth picking up on sale.

So what is B4B exactly? It's a coop zombie survivor game, a re-imagination of and older Valve classic.

B4B feels like a first attempt at achieving escape velocity from their overlords grasp— and does so admirably. Though we shouldn't be surprised— We've seen a few titles/concepts make that jump, to mixed success.

For some, trying to bite that apple has meant being cast out. For others, it has been a well spring of new life. B4B feels like one of those latter examples. However, having said that there are a few things to be aware of.

One: There is a thriving modding community for L4D. So unless you're playing on a console (which I believe is still in service), you get a plethora of odds and ends. Enough to argue that we've already been given a L4D:3.

Two: There is a certain lack of polish with this title. I can't quite put my finger on it, but there IS some sort of disparity between B4B and L4D. Perhaps it's the "new-car-sheen" that has worn off. Or maybe it is something tangible that i cannot place my finger on. I suspect it has something to do with the drabness of the color palate, and my investment in the characters.

Three: The coop aspect of it is less about your team cohesiveness, and more about your team synergy. So you may find yourself arguing less about what you're doing, and more about what you're bringing. If you've played Dead by Daylight you'll know what I mean.

So is it worth a play? Absolutely. (it has had several free-to-play trials, and discounts for the full title). Is it a pre-order quality game? Not for some. But for those of you that bought Cyberpunk, you know the risk. 

SHOULD. YOU. PLAY. IT? Eventually yes, but do not burn your bridges getting there.

The first play-through on Recruit difficulty with friends will last you about 15-20 hours and will be fun (and a bit too easy).  After that the difficulty spikes way too high when playing on the next difficulty up.  This leaves you and your team at an impasse... Do we keep playing Recruit difficulty over and over or do we just quit? We just quit.

A game made by "basically the same people" who gifted the world with Left 4 Dead... yeah all right. That's either a big fat marketing lie (very likely, 13 years later) or Valve had much more do to with the quality of Left 4 Dead than some might think.

Left 4 Dead was a masterpiece and a beautiful piece of art. Back 4 Blood is a cheap knock-off... or to be precise a rather expensive one : this should have been a 30 $ game to my opinion. I think the people behind this game have good ideas and maybe good intentions. Unfortunately they severely lack artistic sense and can't make up for it in quality of execution.

Xbox Game Pass and Crossplay are probably the worst things of all. Those fill the player base with individuals that no Co-op games aficionado wants anything to do with. Fortunately, Crossplay can be disabled.

However, it wouldn't be fair for me to give a thumb down. After 40 trial hours through Game Pass PC, I decided to buy the game with a Steam DRM... and after 50 more hours, I don't think I'm gonna stop playing it any time soon ! The Co-op mechanics are good. The card system is interesting. A map can be a bit different every time you play : it can be night, it can be some fog, the "monsters" can be of a different kind, etc...

I would recommend this product to anybody who likes Co-op games.
